title: WF Inventory — new layout
question: The roll leads with the Trading Blotter. Keep the lead, take one of the other dealt structures, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Trading Blotter
options.lineage: market data sheets and trading blotters
options.thesis: Every owned mod as one sortable ledger row that expands in place into the rich riven/mod card — scan your whole hoard at a glance, open the one that matters.
options.viewport: Header with search and avatar, stat strip (803 mods / 48 rivens) with filter chips, then a dense ruled table; the selected riven row spreads into a full attribute card mid-table.
options.risk: Reads clinical if ranks and wear shrink too far; the expanded row must keep the table rhythm when it opens.

options.label: The Vault
options.thesis: A collector's vault: persistent icon rail, each section a dense card grid under its own running total strip.
options.viewport: Icon rail on the left, section header with counts and filter chips, then a 4-column card grid of owned mods.
options.risk: Repeats the card grid the rest of Quantframe already uses; freshness must come from the section strip and rail.

options.label: The Workbench
options.thesis: Master-detail bench: compact ledger list on the left, the focused item rendered full-size on the right with every stat readable at once.
options.viewport: Header and filter row, then split view: 460px ledger list left, focus pane right showing the selected riven's frame, attribute plaques and actions without any click-through.
options.risk: The right pane can feel oversized for plain mods; it earns its space only while a riven is focused.
